Definition 2.2.1 (scalar extension of algebras and modules)

contents.reason: Tensor-product twists are not used in the scalar-extension orbit argument, the division-algebra comparison, or any of the four designed examples.

Definition 2.3.1 (centralizer)
contents.reason: The planned page uses only the resulting central division algebra and its index, not a separate centralizer calculus for arbitrary subrings.

contents.name: Proposition 2.3.2 (centralizers commute with tensor products)
contents.reason: This general tensor-centralizer identity is not required once the author proves the needed base-change Hom identity directly for finite group representations.

contents.name: Proposition 2.3.3 (scalar extension of a central simple algebra is central simple)
Proposition 2.3.4 (double-centralizer decomposition for a simple subalgebra)
contents.reason: The full double-centralizer theorem would be a separate central-simple-algebra development; this page only needs its scalar matrix consequence in one specialized proof.

contents.name: Theorem 2.3.5 (maximal subfields split a division algebra and have its index degree)
Lemma 2.3.6 (a finite-dimensional division algebra over an algebraically closed field is the field)
Corollary 2.3.7 (maximal subfields are isomorphic)
contents.reason: Uniqueness up to isomorphism of maximal subfields is stronger than the chosen index and minimal-multiplicity route needs, which uses only their degrees and splitting property.

contents.name: Corollary 2.3.8 (Wedderburn: every finite division ring is a field)
contents.reason: The page works throughout in characteristic zero and does not need the finite-division-ring theorem or its finite-field consequence.

contents.name: Corollary 2.3.9 (central simple algebras over algebraically closed or finite fields split)
contents.reason: The algebraically closed case is absorbed in the absolute-irreducibility comparison, while the finite-field case lies outside the page's characteristic-zero convention.

contents.reason: The selected proof route deliberately takes a finite cyclotomic splitting extension, so the non-splitting representation-field refinement is not load-bearing here.

contents.reason: The arithmetic Euler-phi upper bound is not used by the designed general theory or examples, which retain only the direct degree divisibility from scalar extension.
